verdicts.evidence: RECIPE: spec `- AC1 -> file:./` (a pointer to the root itself), `runward spec-check s.md -p . --json`. Before: exit 1, reason 'file:./ — points outside the project tree'; after: exit 1 but reason 'file:./ — not a file' — the remediation changes nature. Measured AGGRAVATING factor: `-p` on a FILE (the CLI does not refuse it) inverts the verdict, exit 1 -> exit 0 'linked'. The dedicated tests only exercise containment through file:../../etc/passwd (the startsWith('..') arm) and never assert its reason; the rel === '' arm is never visited.

Measured: `file:./` goes from 'points outside the project tree' to 'not a file' (exit 1 kept); and with `-p` on a file, complete inversion exit 1 -> 0 'linked'. Missed for the same reason: the only containment test goes through startsWith('..') and only asserts linked === false.

verdicts.evidence: JS semantics: when p.line is undefined, `content.split('\n').length < undefined` is a NaN comparison = false — the && decides identically with the guard forced to true. Measured: 0 diff on the 20 scenarios (function AND CLI), including pointers without :LINE. Measured sensitivity control: the same probe detects mutants 21 and 22 carried by the SAME line (2 diffs each, verdict inversions) — the line is indeed observed, this mutant really has no effect. Only residual cost: a useless split.

verdicts.evidence: VERDICT INVERSION on a quoted symbol padded with spaces. RECIPE: spec `- AC1 -> file:code/short.ts#" x"` (symbol ' x', 2 characters one of which is whitespace, trim -> 1), artifact 'const x = 1;', spec-check --json. Before: exit 1, 'names no usable symbol'; after: exit 0, 'linked' via content.includes(' x') — a pseudo-symbol made of one whitespace + one letter matches almost everywhere. Only the QUOTED form can carry whitespace and no test writes one: the trim is never discriminated.
